screening_results.reason: The NeuroStore record reports only a within-group voxelwise regression among PTSD patients (n=15) relating symptom severity to gray matter volume; no control group or PTSD vs control between-group contrasts are reported. Therefore the study does not meet full-text inclusion criteria I1 (requires GM volume differences between PTSD and controls) and I2 (requires at least one whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast). Exclusion criterion E5 (only within-group results without a qualifying between-group contrast) applies.

Meets I1 (empirical English MRI VBM study comparing GM volume between PTSD patients and controls), I2 (reports at least one whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM contrast), I3 (results reported in tables/coordinates), and I4 (controls are trauma-exposed survivors without PTSD). No exclusion criteria (E1-E6) are met based on the record.

Meets full-text inclusion criteria: I1 empirical English MRI VBM study comparing GM volume between PTSD patients and controls; I2 reports whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrasts (VBM in SPM2, whole-brain); I3 results reported as peaks/tables; I4 controls are trauma-exposed (matched fire victims) without PTSD. No full-text exclusion criteria are met based on the NeuroStore record.

The NeuroStore record describes a whole-brain VBM study of 27 combat-exposed individuals without PTSD (no participant met full PDS criteria). Analyses are cross-subject within-group regressions relating days of deployment to GM volume; no between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing PTSD patients to controls are reported. Therefore inclusion criteria I1 (study of PTSD patients vs controls) and I2 (at least one whole-brain between-group contrast of PTSD vs controls) are not met. I3 (allowing results reported in tables/figures/supplement) is met (reported peaks present). Exclusion criteria E5 (only within-group results with no between-group PTSD vs control contrast) applies; E3 (study of trauma-exposed individuals without PTSD rather than PTSD patients) also applies.

NeuroStore record reports only within-group, cross-subject voxelwise regressions in a single cohort (n=32, 15 meeting current PTSD criteria) and does not report any whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts of PTSD patients versus controls. Therefore full-text inclusion criteria I1 and I2 (between-group GM comparisons of PTSD vs controls) are not met; exclusion criterion E5 (studies reporting only within-group results without a qualifying between-group contrast) applies.

Meets full-text inclusion criteria: I1 empirical English MRI VBM study comparing GM volume between PTSD patients and controls (victims with PTSD vs matched victims without PTSD); I2 reports at least one whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrast (Analysis 12853571_analysis_0 listed as whole-brain, between-group); I3 reporting of results (peaks) is present; I4 control group is trauma-exposed victims without PTSD. No full-text exclusion criteria from the record are met.

Meets full-text inclusion criteria: I1 (empirical MRI study of GM volume comparing PTSD patients and controls), I2 (reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts of PTSD patients vs controls — e.g., Analysis 23155380_analysis_0), I3 (results reported as tables/peaks), I4 (controls are healthy or trauma-exposed and acceptable). No exclusion criteria from E1–E6 are met by the NeuroStore record.

The NeuroStore record indicates an empirical MRI morphometric study comparing PTSD patients and healthy controls (I1). The analysis reports a whole-brain voxelwise grey matter density contrast (spatial scope: whole brain) with reported peak coordinates (I2, I3). Controls are healthy participants, acceptable as control group (I4). No exclusion criteria (E1-E6) are met based on the record.

Record indicates an empirical VBM study of gray matter volume comparing PTSD patients and controls (I1). NeuroStore lists 'Spatial scope: whole brain' and between-group contrasts comparing PTSD vs non-PTSD and vs healthy controls, satisfying whole-brain evidence (I2). Results are reported (peaks) and acceptable if in tables/figures (I3). Control groups include both non-PTSD cancer survivors and healthy subjects (I4). The record does mention ROI/SVC corrections at the analysis level, but the shared metadata explicitly states whole-brain spatial scope; therefore the study meets the full-text inclusion criteria. No full-text incompleteness is indicated.

I1 met: empirical English MRI study assessing GM volume differences (manual tracing showed smaller amygdala in PTSD-history group). I3 met (results reported). I4 met (controls include trauma-exposed without PTSD). I2 NOT met: the NeuroStore record does not report any whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrast of PTSD patients vs controls comparing GM volume; instead the listed voxelwise analyses are within-group correlations and diagnosis×volume interactions. Therefore exclusion E5 applies: no qualifying between-group PTSD vs control voxelwise contrast is reported.

The study is a longitudinal VBM study in clinically healthy adults relating number of stressful life events (SLEs) to GMV; it does not include PTSD patients or a between-group PTSD vs control comparison (I1 not met). The reported analysis uses a region-of-interest (pre-defined mask) rather than a whole-brain voxelwise contrast (I2 not met). Thus it addresses SLEs in a non-PTSD sample and lacks qualifying whole-brain PTSD-control contrasts.

Study reports an empirical English-language structural MRI VBM analysis comparing pediatric PTSD patients and matched controls, reporting whole-brain voxelwise gray matter density/volume differences (PTSD > controls). Controls are healthy matched individuals. The NeuroStore record indicates whole-brain voxelwise results (SPM) with reported peaks. All inclusion criteria I1, I2, I3, and I4 are met; no exclusion criteria are met based on the record.

The NeuroStore record indicates the sample comprises healthy, non-clinical participants comparing FKBP5 genotype groups, not PTSD patients vs controls. Therefore the study does not meet full-text inclusion criteria I1 (must assess GM differences between PTSD patients and controls) and I2 (must report at least one whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrast of PTSD patients vs controls). The record does not state any PTSD patient vs control comparison.

Meets inclusion criteria: I1 empirical MRI study of GM volume differences between PTSD patients and controls; I2 reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (Controls > PTSD) of GM volume; I3 reported results include peaks/tables; I4 controls are healthy participants. No full-text exclusion criteria are met based on the NeuroStore record.

The NeuroStore record indicates the sample consists of healthy adults with childhood maltreatment (CTQ) measures and reports within-group regression analyses and an ROI hippocampus analysis of gray matter volume. The record contains no PTSD patient group or any between-group voxelwise PTSD vs control contrasts required by inclusion criteria I1 and I2. Therefore exclusion criteria E3 (studies not specifically measuring PTSD) and E5 (only within-group analyses without PTSD vs control contrasts) apply.

I1 met: the record includes empirical MRI VBM gray matter volume analyses. I4 met: control group includes healthy/trauma-exposed individuals acceptable. I2 NOT met: the NeuroStore record does not report any whole-brain voxelwise between-group (PTSD vs controls) contrast of gray matter volume that is whole-brain corrected. The only between-group VBM analysis (analysis_26441695_analysis_0) is reported with small-volume/ROI FWE correction (SVC), and other VBM analyses are within-group or the VBM-labelled analyses report perfusion measures in the record, so there is no qualifying whole-brain between-group GM contrast. This meets exclusion E1 (only ROI/SVC analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results).

Record indicates an empirical VBM study in English assessing grey matter differences in PTSD (I1). Spatial scope is listed as whole brain and there are between-group contrasts of PTSD patients vs controls (I2). Results are reported as coordinates/tables (I3). Control groups include healthy and trauma-exposed without PTSD (I4). No exclusion criteria (E1-E6) are indicated by the record.

The NeuroStore record reports a whole-brain within-group regression (self-blame vs GMV) in sexually assaulted participants and lists non-exposed matched controls, but it does NOT report any whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrast of PTSD patients vs controls. Therefore full-text inclusion criteria I2 (whole-brain between-group PTSD vs controls contrast) is not met, and I1 (study assessing GM volume differences between PTSD patients and controls) is not met as framed (no between-group comparisons reported). The record does show reported peaks (so I3 is met) and uses an acceptable control population (I4 is met). Exclusion criterion E5 applies (studies reporting only within-group results without a qualifying between-group contrast).

The NeuroStore record shows this study performed diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) analyses (TBSS/FA) examining white matter integrity and ROI correlations; it does not report any voxelwise whole-brain grey matter (GM) volume between-group contrasts (VBM) comparing PTSD patients and controls. Therefore full-text inclusion criteria I1 (GM volume MRI) and I2 (whole-brain voxelwise GM between-group contrast) are not met. The record does indicate both healthy and trauma-exposed control groups, so I4 is met. No full-text exclusion criteria (E1–E6) from the provided list are explicitly met by the record.

The NeuroStore record reports cortical thickness (structural morphometry) rather than grey matter (GM) volume; therefore full-text inclusion criteria I1 (GM volume differences) and I2 (whole-brain voxelwise contrast comparing GM volume) are not met. The record does meet I3 (acceptable reporting in tables/figures) and I4 (appropriate control population). No full-text exclusion criteria are met.

Record reports an empirical VBM (MRI) study comparing PTSD patients and controls (I1). At least one whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM contrast PTSD vs controls is reported (Analysis 19942229_analysis_0; I2). Results are reported in tables of peaks and described in the abstract (I3). Control group consists of trauma-exposed individuals without PTSD/healthy participants, which is acceptable (I4). No full-text exclusion criteria (E1–E6) are met based on the record.

Meets inclusion criteria: I1 empirical MRI study of GM differences between PTSD patients and controls (measure: gray matter density); I2 reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (analysis_0 reports voxel-level uncorrected p<.001 across whole brain); I3 results are reported as tables of peaks; I4 control groups include non-PTSD (trauma-exposed and unexposed) which are acceptable. No exclusion criteria from E1–E6 are met based on the NeuroStore record.

Meets I1: empirical MRI study assessing GM volume differences between PTSD patients and controls (VBM and SIENAX described). Meets I2: reports at least one whole-brain voxelwise between-group VBM contrast (whole-brain, corrected, reported peaks). Meets I3: results reported in table of peaks (Table 3). Meets I4: controls are matched non‑traumatized healthy participants. No full-text exclusion criteria (E1–E6) are met based on the record.

The NeuroStore record reports whole-brain VBM analyses of GM volume in PTSD patients, but all reported analyses are comparisons within the PTSD sample (dissociative vs non-dissociative) or correlations with symptom measures. The record contains no between-group voxelwise whole-brain PTSD patients vs controls contrasts. Therefore the study does not meet inclusion criteria I1 and I2. Exclusion E5 (only within-group results without a qualifying PTSD vs control contrast) applies.

The NeuroStore record shows this is an empirical MRI study including structural morphometry analyses, but it does not report any voxelwise whole-brain between-group (PTSD patients vs controls) comparisons of gray matter volume. The structural analyses (analysis_8 and analysis_9) are cross-subject within-group regressions relating CTQ to GM volume in PTSD patients. Many other reported analyses are functional/connectivity and ROI. Therefore full-text inclusion criteria I1 and I2 (PTSD vs control whole-brain GM comparisons) are not met. This meets exclusion criterion E5 (studies reporting only within-group results in PTSD patients without a qualifying between-group contrast).

The NeuroStore record describes a treatment-outcome study comparing responders vs non-responders within a PTSD sample (no healthy or trauma-exposed control group). Therefore full-text inclusion criteria I1 (PTSD vs controls) and I2 (whole-brain voxelwise PTSD vs control contrast) are not met. The study is a treatment/longitudinal study without a qualifying PTSD vs control between-group contrast (E4) and reports only within-PTSD-group comparisons (responders vs non-responders) without PTSD vs control contrasts (E5). Full text appears available from the record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The record shows this is an empirical VBM study comparing PTSD patients and controls (I1 met). Results are reported in tables/abstract (I3 met) and controls are acceptable (I4 met). However, all reported analyses are ROI-based (spatial scope: region of interest; hippocampal/amygdala mask and hippocampal ROIs) and no whole-brain voxelwise between-group GMV contrast is reported in the NeuroStore record, so full-text inclusion criterion I2 is not met. This meets exclusion criterion E1 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results).

Meets I1 (empirical MRI study of GM volume differences between PTSD and controls), I2 (reports at least one whole-brain voxel-wise between-group GM volume contrast: Analysis 30343133_analysis_0 TD > PTSD), I3 (results reported as table peaks), and I4 (controls are nontraumatized typically developing youths). No exclusion criteria are met based on the NeuroStore record.

The study reports empirical VBM structural MRI results including PTSD patients (n=91) and healthy controls, and the abstract states voxelwise whole-brain group comparisons (FWE-corrected) showing effects for the four psychiatric groups relative to healthy controls. This satisfies I1 (MRI VBM comparing GM in PTSD) and I2 (whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts reported), with I3 and I4 also met (results reported in main text/abstract; controls are healthy). The NeuroStore record does not list a specific PTSD>HC whole-brain analysis entry, but the abstract explicitly indicates that each diagnostic group (including PTSD) was compared to healthy controls with whole-brain VBM results, so I2 is considered met. No exclusion criteria from E1-E6 are met based on the record.

The NeuroStore record describes structural MRI and gray matter density measures in PTSD patients and controls, but it does not report any whole-brain voxel-wise between-group (PTSD vs control) contrasts of grey matter volume. Instead the reported analysis is a within-group cross-subject regression (correlation between P300 amplitude and GM density) in the PTSD group only. Therefore the study fails to meet I1 (does not clearly report GM volume differences between PTSD and controls) and I2 (no whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrast). It does meet I4 (controls are trauma-exposed victims without PTSD). The available record also indicates only within-group results, meeting exclusion E5 (studies that report only within-group results without a qualifying between-group contrast).

Meets I1 (empirical English MRI VBM study reporting GM volume differences between PTSD patients and controls), I2 (reports whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrasts), I3 (results reported as tables of coordinates), and I4 (uses both healthy and trauma-exposed control groups). No exclusion criteria from E1–E6 are met based on the NeuroStore record.

The study examines trauma-exposed firefighters without PTSD and does not report comparisons involving PTSD patients. Therefore it fails full-text inclusion criteria I1 (must assess PTSD patients) and I2 (must report at least one whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast of PTSD patients vs controls). The record does show neuroimaging results reported as peak coordinates in tables (meets I3). The study is about trauma-exposed individuals without PTSD, so exclusion criterion E3 applies.

Record indicates an empirical voxel-based morphometry study in English with gray matter volume measures comparing PTSD patients to controls using whole-brain voxelwise analyses (multiple regression across trauma-exposed adults and within PTSD group). The analysis includes whole-brain voxel-wise GMV (GLOBAL_I1) and a between-group contrast is implied in the abstract describing associations with PTSD diagnosis; however, NeuroStore record shows one analysis is a within-group regression in PTSD patients (no direct patients vs controls contrast). Inclusion criteria I1 and I2: The study assesses GM volume; whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported. The record does not explicitly state a direct between-group patients vs controls contrast; it describes interaction and regression including diagnosis, and the analysis extracted is within-group regression in patients only. Because the abstract mentions diagnosis-by-social support interaction across trauma-exposed adults (implying between-group effects) but the only extracted analysis is within-group, the record is incomplete regarding between-group contrasts; but the study as a whole reports voxelwise comparisons involving diagnosis per abstract. Given the meta-analysis objective (PTSD vs controls), and that NeuroStore record does not clearly provide a between-group contrast, I include the study but mark fulltext_incomplete=false because the document could be read (not unreadable). Inclusion criteria applied: I1, I2, I3, I4. Exclusion criteria applied: none met.

Meets I1 (empirical English MRI study assessing GM volume differences between PTSD and controls). Meets I2 because the record includes a whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast (Analysis 23021615_analysis_2: Non-PTSD>PTSD). I3 is satisfied (results reported in tables/analyses). I4 is satisfied (control group are non-PTSD trauma-exposed individuals). No full-text incompleteness shown in the record. No exclusion criteria (E1–E6) appear to apply from the record.

The NeuroStore record indicates the sample consists entirely of healthy participants with no subject meeting PTSD criteria; the study examines associations between post-traumatic growth (PTG) and longitudinal delta-rGMV within those individuals (voxelwise regressions), not voxelwise between-group PTSD patients vs controls comparisons. Therefore full-text inclusion criteria I1 (MRI studies comparing PTSD patients and controls) and I2 (at least one whole-brain voxelwise between-group PTSD vs control contrast) are not met. The record shows a trauma-related longitudinal study without a qualifying PTSD vs control contrast, so exclusion criteria E3 (trauma study not specifically measuring PTSD) and E4 (longitudinal study without a qualifying between-group PTSD vs control contrast) apply. fulltext_incomplete=false.

The NeuroStore record describes a voxel-based morphometry study of borderline personality disorder (BPD) patients versus healthy controls. PTSD is only measured as a comorbidity/covariate within the BPD sample (some patients have current or lifetime PTSD); there are no analyses that compare PTSD patients to healthy controls or report whole-brain voxelwise GM differences specifically between PTSD patients and controls. Therefore the study does not meet full-text inclusion criteria I1 and I2 (does not assess GM volume differences between PTSD patients and controls and contains no whole-brain PTSD vs control contrasts). The record does not indicate the article could not be read (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The NeuroStore record shows empirical MRI morphometry comparisons of gray matter volume between PTSD patients and healthy controls, including whole-brain voxelwise between-group baseline contrasts (patients > controls and patients < controls). Controls are healthy participants. Although the study also reports longitudinal/treatment analyses, the presence of baseline whole-brain between-group contrasts satisfies inclusion. No exclusion criteria from E1-E6 apply based on the record.

The NeuroStore record indicates this is an empirical study of healthy adolescents relating maternal interpersonal affiliation to adolescents' brain structure and reward-related BOLD responses. It does not include PTSD patients or PTSD vs control between-group voxelwise GM volume contrasts. Therefore full-text inclusion criteria I1 (MRI studies assessing GM volume differences between PTSD patients and controls) and I2 (at least one whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrast of PTSD patients vs controls comparing GM volume) are not met.

The NeuroStore record describes a longitudinal treatment study of PTSD patients (responders vs non-responders) with voxel-based morphometry within patients over time. The record does not report any between-group whole-brain voxelwise comparisons of PTSD patients versus a control group (healthy or trauma-exposed). Therefore the study does not meet full-text inclusion criteria I1 and I2 (no PTSD vs control between-group GMV contrasts). It meets exclusion criteria E4 (treatment/longitudinal study without a qualifying PTSD vs control contrast) and E5 (only within-group results / comparisons between patient subgroups, no PTSD vs control contrast). Full text appears readable from the record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

NeuroStore record shows this is an empirical VBM study comparing PTSD patients and trauma-exposed controls (I1 met) and reports peaks (I3 met). Controls are trauma-exposed individuals (I4 met). However the record indicates 'Spatial scope: region of interest' and the reported regions are hippocampus and anterior cingulate (ROI), so it does not provide a voxelwise whole-brain between-group contrast required by I2. Therefore exclusion E1 (ROI-only analyses) applies and the study does not meet I2.

The NeuroStore record reports only within-group voxelwise regressions in a PTSD patient sample (associations with reexperiencing/flashback scores) and lists no control group or any between-group PTSD vs control contrasts. Therefore full-text inclusion criteria I1 and I2 (between-group GM volume comparisons vs controls; whole-brain) are not met. This matches exclusion criterion E5 (studies reporting only within-group results).

The NeuroStore record indicates all reported analyses use a spatial scope of 'region of interest' (ACC gyrus defined by atlas) rather than voxelwise whole-brain analyses. Full-text inclusion criterion I2 (must report at least one whole-brain voxel-wise between-group GM volume contrast of PTSD patients vs controls) is not met. The study is an empirical MRI morphometry study comparing PTSD patients and controls (I1 met) and uses acceptable control populations (I4 met). However, because all analyses are ROI-limited, exclusion criterion E1 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results) applies. The record provides peaks/results, so E6 (only null results) does not apply. Full text appears sufficiently captured in the record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

I1 met: NeuroStore record indicates an empirical MRI study measuring gray matter volume in PTSD patients. I2 NOT met: the record shows only a region-of-interest (ROI) analysis and no whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts. Therefore GLOBAL_E1 (ROI-only analyses) applies and the study is excluded.

The NeuroStore record indicates analyses are reported as region-of-interest (masked VBM) within orbitofrontal cortex, amygdala, hippocampus, and ACC. Analysis 0 explicitly has 'Spatial scope: region of interest'. No analysis in the record provides evidence of an unmasked voxelwise whole-brain between-group GM contrast. Therefore the record meets I1, I3, and I4 but does not meet I2, and E1 applies (only ROI analyses reported).

The record shows this is an empirical MRI VBM study of gray matter (I1 met) reporting whole-brain analyses in general, and uses healthy controls (I4 met). However, the only between-group PTSD vs control contrast (Analysis 21418787_analysis_0) is reported with a small volume correction / corrected within ROI (SVC), so the record does not provide a qualifying whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrast (I2 not met). Because the paper therefore effectively reports only ROI/SVC-corrected between-group results with no whole-brain contrast, it meets exclusion criterion E1.
